original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove a sharp rank-mass obstruction s >= 2W for arbitrary deterministic finite-alphabet permutation circuits whose rational two-dimensional frames lie in {0,I,J,J+I,B,B+I}, the seed proposed by PR1757 with its identity translates.
scope_change_reason: The current card suggests a larger/nonabelian register alphabet. The live source question in PR1757 instead supplies a specific non-common-flag rational frame seed and asks for a five-role cost at most nine. This contribution changes to a source-specific alphabet obstruction using its cited weighted partition theorem, not another three-register census.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result for the search for a contracting nonlinear finite shear circuit. It rules out the proposed six-frame seed at every circuit size and therefore prevents further topology search inside this alphabet from beating its rank-mass bill. It supplies no BIT or complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship the first new exact cut certificate after a written proof and bounded local replay; do not enlarge the frame alphabet or seek a stronger theorem.
evidence: README.md proves s >= 2W by applying PR1757 to the two explicitly certified binary partitions. verify.py checks 36 ordered exact ranks with two rank algorithms, all three identity shifts, all 4096 binary-pair label assignments, and 11 rejecting controls. Receipts are computed on stdout and bind all five package files and the predecessor bytes.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which additional rational frame destroys the two-cut certificate while retaining an attainable five-role cost at most nine?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Non-common-flag geometry alone does not escape this new alphabet-specific obstruction. A changed frame alphabet is necessary before the source topology search can succeed.
open_questions.first_step: Add one proposed rational frame to the six-frame distance table, include every available identity-shift demand, and solve the weighted partition feasibility problem before searching circuit words.
open_questions.blocked_by: Failure of this particular two-cut certificate is not a construction or a proof that no other weighted cut certificate exists.

open_questions.question: Can a complete nonlinear permutation circuit outside this alphabet achieve s < 2W?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Such a witness would move beyond both the common-flag class and the newly excluded seed, and is a prerequisite for a favorable optimistic concave rank bill.
open_questions.first_step: Publish one finite DAG with full truth-table semantics, one common rational frame per gate, every physical edge and the exact source/sink identity shifts.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present result supplies no changed-alphabet circuit, physical supplier, compiler or complete invoice.

coordination.coverage: Live open PR bodies and discussions through the overlap cache; all main README paths additionally searched by git grep. Arbitrary code diffs and unpublished work are not covered.

claim_type: scoped mathematical proof with exact finite certificate
